claim: When two packages build in parallel against a wire contract, type every response envelope (the {items: [...]} wrapper) in the shared contract and hold it with a parity test, because a contract that types only the items lets each side guess the wrapper and both sides test green against their own guess.
because: athena-meta: the daemon answered {spaces},{turns},{cards}; the client built in parallel read bare arrays; 89 py + 36 ts tests passed; caught in Director review, fixed by envelope types + parity test.

claim: When a validation door shows its drop reasons to the end user, write them in the surface vocabulary, not the spec vocabulary, because the reasons are UI copy and any banned-word or plain-language rule applies to them too.
because: business Phase 1: the door wrote reasons naming block/binding/records; the UI builder found them through a banned-word test and the Director rewrote 18 reason strings in validate.py.

claim: When an unattended cycle reads web pages for a model to extract items, hand the model the page links with their addresses alongside the visible text, because visible text carries no URLs and the model will otherwise drop or invent the identifiers it must key records by.
because: business Phase 2 seam on the built shell: 4 uploads seen, 0 kept, and a reply sent to a guessed address; adding a page_links hand took the seam from 3/9 to 9/9.

claim: When comparing two LLM engines on a multi-turn product flow, drive the real UI with a fixed persona model, strip engine and model names from each transcript, and grade before unblinding, because the grader's prior about which engine is weaker otherwise decides ambiguous cases.
because: onboarding-engine-parity: blind grades put the expected-weaker engine level (3.24 vs 3.20) and attributed a blocker to the expected-stronger engine; both shared defects were in the daemon, not the model.

claim: When a model call produces structured output that a validator rejects, keep the raw answer on disk (newest few) and feed the parse error with its surrounding text back in the repair prompt, because a bare "not valid" repair repeats the same mistake and the failure looks unreproducible without the artefact.
because: onboarding-jobs: a writing failure seen twice and unreproduced was, once answers were kept, a whole JSON one brace short (fixed by closing brackets at the end); a second engine repeated a mid-answer extra brace three times under a count-your-brackets hint.
